questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Prior exposure and the asymmetry of a first epidemic
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a first epidemic in a naive population is more severe than later waves
questions.stem: A Pacific island had no measles before 1875, then suffered a devastating first outbreak; why was the first wave so much worse than later ones?

options.text: Earlier exposure would have left survivors with lasting immunity
The virus mutated into a milder strain between waves
options.misconception: assumes mutation rather than host immunity changed severity

options.text: Medical care improved only after the first wave ended
options.misconception: confuses timing of care with biological susceptibility

questions.explanation: A first epidemic in a fully susceptible population kills more because no one has prior immunity, while later waves meet immune survivors; climate and mutation are not the main driver.
